purpose: User-facing capability register. This is not the internal actor capability registry; it exists so release value starts from what a user can do.

capabilities.name: Traceability
capabilities.description: AOF can link work, requirements, sessions, decisions, evidence, and release readiness into an auditable chain.
capabilities.user_value: Users can reconstruct why work exists and what evidence supports it without reading every raw artifact.

capabilities.name: Organization Memory
capabilities.description: AOF can keep canonical state for tasks, goals, runtime sessions, decisions, artifacts, and learning updates.
capabilities.user_value: Users can continue governed work across sessions instead of relying on one long chat transcript.

capabilities.name: Governance
capabilities.description: AOF can separate maker work, checker review, council judgment, and release gates.
capabilities.user_value: Users can stop work from being called done only because the maker says it is done.

capabilities.name: Human Approval
capabilities.description: AOF can record independent human approval and revocation state for external-write candidates.
capabilities.user_value: Users can distinguish Council review from explicit human permission before external side effects.

capabilities.name: External Resource Access
capabilities.description: AOF can represent external actors, tools, providers, and references with source-of-truth and permission boundaries.
capabilities.user_value: Users can see what external resource is being used, for what purpose, and under what limits.

capabilities.name: Provider Execution
capabilities.description: AOF can model provider execution readiness, approval, reproduction, rollback, outcome, learning, production-boundary candidates, controlled execution candidates, incident recovery, and cost/quota boundaries.
capabilities.user_value: Users can see when a provider-backed action is only a controlled candidate and cannot be confused with production execution.

capabilities.name: Provider Incident Recovery
capabilities.description: AOF can record and audit a provider incident drill that links a controlled execution candidate to detection, containment, rollback, recovery, notification, learning, and resume/stop governance.
capabilities.user_value: Users can inspect what happens if a provider-backed action fails before allowing the action to advance.

capabilities.name: Provider Cost/Quota Boundary
capabilities.description: AOF can record and audit provider execution spend and quota boundaries that bind budget owner, budget period, cost ceiling, token/call/retry caps, quota, rate limit, billing, overage policy, and stop governance.
capabilities.user_value: Users can see whether provider-backed execution is allowed to spend tokens, calls, quota, or money before execution advances.

capabilities.name: Rollback
capabilities.description: AOF can require rollback readiness evidence before provider execution claims are trusted.
capabilities.user_value: Users can avoid treating an external operation as acceptable when reversal evidence is missing.

capabilities.name: Learning
capabilities.description: AOF can convert outcome evidence into an accepted, corrected, rollback, escalation, or defer learning update.
capabilities.user_value: Users can make the next decision depend on what happened, rather than losing feedback after release.

capabilities.name: Product Value Comprehension
capabilities.description: AOF can require release value evidence that states what a user can now do, before/after, demo, reduced work, and not-proven boundaries.
capabilities.user_value: Users do not need to infer release value from records, audits, schemas, or dashboard existence.

capabilities.name: Capability-First Release
capabilities.description: AOF can require a formal capability register, version matrix, capability delta, and release acceptance criteria before release-ready claims.
capabilities.user_value: Users can understand what changed in a release within 30 seconds before reading implementation details.

capabilities.name: Archmap Lifecycle Traceability
capabilities.description: AOF can map governed work, requirements, acceptance criteria, decisions, risks, tests, and evidence into the Archmap v0.4 lifecycle provider baseline without making Archmap the source of truth.
capabilities.user_value: Users can inspect where architecture and work evidence fit in the lifecycle view instead of manually connecting separate AOF artifacts.

capabilities.name: Production Go/No-Go Evidence
capabilities.description: AOF can bundle provider execution readiness evidence into a bounded operator-facing production go/no-go candidate without authorizing live execution.
capabilities.user_value: Users can make a production-readiness judgment from one evidence surface instead of manually assembling approval, reproduction, rollback, outcome, incident, and cost/quota records.

capabilities.name: Production Readiness Review
capabilities.description: AOF can present a bounded review of whether external runtime provider-backed work is ready for human production go/no-go judgment.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can decide what is missing before production movement without reading every provider artifact manually.

capabilities.name: External Runtime Productization Decision
capabilities.description: AOF can decide whether external runtime evidence is coherent enough to advance as a product-grade capability surface.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can distinguish productization readiness from live execution permission and know what validation remains.

capabilities.name: Third-Party Operator Validation Contract
capabilities.description: AOF can define what an external operator must verify before external runtime claims can move beyond self-hosting evidence.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can see exactly what outside validation must prove and what remains unproven.

capabilities.name: External Provider Pilot Selection
capabilities.description: AOF can select a bounded first external provider pilot candidate with rationale, alternatives, and blocked conditions before integration starts.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can understand which provider AOF should pilot first and why, without mistaking selection for integration or execution.

capabilities.name: Production Execution Authorization Model
capabilities.description: Defines the approval, authority, budget, rollback, incident, stop, reproduction, and adapter-capability gates required before live provider execution can be allowed.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can block unsafe live provider actions until every required authorization gate exists and is reviewed.

capabilities.name: External Value Reproduction Evidence Package
capabilities.description: AOF can prepare a bounded package for an external operator to reproduce and report user-visible value.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can test AOF value outside self-hosting without mistaking internal artifacts for external proof.

capabilities.name: Provider-Backed Work Lifecycle Product Surface
capabilities.description: AOF can explain provider-backed work as a user-facing lifecycle from Need to blocked or ready next action.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can understand provider-backed work without stitching raw artifacts together.

capabilities.name: Third-Party Validation Result Ingestion
capabilities.description: AOF can normalize and govern third-party validation results against capability claims.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can turn external reviewer feedback into traceable governance evidence without treating it as automatic approval.

capabilities.name: Capability Coverage Gate
capabilities.description: Block build/release-critical work when required roles, skills, concrete actor assignments, output contracts, evidence, acceptance gates, or Council follow-up tasks are missing.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can catch missing specialists before build instead of discovering role/skill gaps during playtest or release review.

capabilities.name: Role Routing Fail-Closed Runtime
capabilities.description: Resolve every required Council role to a concrete actor before execution and stop before persistence when a required specialist cannot be routed.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can require domain specialists such as Game Planner, UX, Level Designer, or QA and trust AOF not to silently skip them.

capabilities.name: Provider Pilot Execution Readiness
capabilities.description: AOF can bundle provider adapter, pilot, approval, target, reproduction, rollback, outcome, learning, operator acceptance, production boundary, controlled candidate, incident recovery, cost/quota, product value, and release-state evidence into one pre-execution readiness decision.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can decide whether a provider-backed pilot is structurally ready to advance without confusing readiness with live provider execution permission.

capabilities.name: GitHub Read-Only Observation Proof
capabilities.description: AOF can inspect real GitHub repository state in read-only mode, compare it with local runtime and roadmap state, and select one next most important task with evidence, Go/No-Go, and no-write boundaries.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can ask what should happen next and receive a concrete Japanese answer grounded in GitHub state without granting write authority.

capabilities.name: External Operator Reproduction Proof
capabilities.description: AOF can provide a bounded five-minute Japanese replay path so a first-time or external operator can understand and reproduce a next-task judgment.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can decide whether AOF's next-task judgment is acceptable without reading the entire repository or asking the AI to explain again.

capabilities.name: Provider Read Integration Proof
capabilities.description: AOF can represent a real external provider read as governed runtime work with adapter/resource refs, observed provider output, no-write boundaries, decision output, evidence refs, and a release audit gate.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can confirm that AOF read GitHub through a bounded no-write path and can inspect the provider output that informed the next decision.

capabilities.name: External Validation Replay
capabilities.description: AOF can represent an external validation result, replay it against provider-read evidence, update confidence before/after, and route uncertainty into governance.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can see whether validation strengthened, weakened, blocked, or escalated a provider-read claim instead of trusting a prose summary.

capabilities.name: Agent Session Contract and Tool Governance Evidence
capabilities.description: AOF can treat an agent session as release-ready evidence only when prompts, responses, tool calls, task links, requirement links, test evidence, risk candidates, decision candidates, stop conditions, and tool authority are explicit and auditable.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can see whether an AI work session is genuinely governed instead of trusting that tool calls happened safely.

capabilities.name: Human-readable Provider Observation Replay
capabilities.description: Replay provider read evidence in operator-readable language with proof boundaries.
capabilities.user_value: Operators can understand provider evidence without reconstructing raw JSON.
